s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with exertion, associated with evidence of myocardial ischemia
salient_findings: Substernal chest pain triggered by running more than 2 miles
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI
key_facts: Hypertension controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
High exercise capacity during treadmill test
Chest pain absent during exercise treadmill test
ST depressions occurred during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
PET-MPI showed severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries

shortlist.label: Three-vessel obstructive coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: CCTA showed 3-vessel involvement and PET-MPI showed severe ischemia

shortlist.label: Chronic stable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has exertional chest pain and evidence of myocardial ischemia on treadmill test

shortlist.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe ischemia on PET-MPI and evidence of coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has high LDL and evidence of coronary artery disease on CCTA and coronary angiogram

shortlist.label: Unstable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test, indicating unstable coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and test results, including the CCTA showing 3-vessel involvement and PET-MPI showing severe ischemia, are most consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic stable angina
rejected.why: While the patient has angina-like symptoms, the presence of 3-vessel involvement and severe ischemia suggests a more complex condition.

rejected.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of reduced ejection fraction or heart failure symptoms, which are typical of cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
rejected.why: This is a broader category that encompasses the champion diagnosis, but is less specific.

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are more consistent with stable angina, as they are triggered by exertion and relieved by rest.
